payload.explanation: pick_hex_red is a step_id NOT on the expected process map -- it is unplanned, and is named here as such. It names object_ids=["hex_red"], but hex_red is listed under this task's BYSTANDERS: the other assembly's part, never picked or placed by this task, with a standing requirement (raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m = 0.02 m) that it never move. My continuously-armed monitor mon_5d69110ee780 (armed at run start on hex_red's rest pose) fired when hex_red's position diverged 0.0241 m from that rest pose. I corroborated with get_evidence over object_poses[hex_red] bracketing the fire: hex_red sat essentially motionless at z=0.0749 m through 1792543326446515700, then rose smoothly to z=0.0804, 0.0906, 0.1165, 0.1416 m across the next four ticks -- a clean, monotonic lift trajectory, not sensor noise or a graze. A look() at the time shows the arm over the right side of the table where hex_red rests. The executor's own end_step for pick_hex_red claims a deliberate, successful grasp-and-lift (final_width_m=0.028 vs expected 0.03, final_effort=36.2, lift_height_m=0.3, claimed_outcome=success) -- this is not an accidental tap but the executor intentionally picking and lifting the bystander hex_red, carrying it well past the 0.02 m disturbance tolerance this task requires for every object it does not act on. Mechanism: the executor appears to have grasped and is now manipulating hex_red (an object outside this task's object set) instead of, or in addition to, proceeding to u_orange -- a direct violation of the undisturbed-bystander requirement, not a borderline case I judged within bounds.

payload.claimed_outcome: executor claimed "aborted": all four base1 parts (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) seated successfully within tolerance, but an interleaved hex_red-into-hex_red_hole insertion (not part of this task) failed after three attempts and hex_red ended off-target.
payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering every step observed from run start through run_ended (status "aborted"). All four of this task's parts reached their required end-state: at my own query_snapshot taken just before run_ended, u_brown (0.0021 m from u_brown_placement, tol 0.01), u_orange (0.0023 m, tol 0.02), line_green (0.00996 m, tol 0.015) and inverted_u_yellow (0.00265 m, tol 0.012) were each within tolerance with matching orientation, and each part's own prior part (u_brown/u_orange/line_green) and base1 stayed within the 0.02 m disturbance tolerance across the subsequent place steps (0.0012-0.0029 m observed). Each place step's grasp-effort-plateau evidence (26.1, 46.3, steady contact signatures) confirmed genuine grasps, not air grasps, and no invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous or in-hand-slippage monitor ever fired for any of the four parts. So considered alone, this task's four-part assembly is conformant.

However, an unplanned step pick_hex_red (not on the expected process map, named here as such) began partway through the run and the executor picked and lifted hex_red -- one of the explicitly-listed BYSTANDERS belonging to the other assembly, which this task requires to never move. My continuously-armed monitor mon_5d69110ee780 fired when hex_red moved 0.024 m from its rest pose, corroborated by a clean monotonic lift trajectory in object_poses and the executor's own end_step claiming a deliberate successful grasp-and-lift (recorded as a finding under pick_hex_red). The executor then ran further unplanned steps (place_approach_hex_red, place_hex_red) attempting to insert hex_red into hex_red_hole on base2 (the other assembly's fixture), retrying three times, and its own place_hex_red end_step reports claimed_outcome "failure": hex_red was never seated and came loose on release, ending up far from both its target and its original rest position. My own final query_snapshot confirms this: hex_red sits at approximately (-0.429, -0.098, 0.019), about 0.57 m from its original rest pose (0.115, 0.039, 0.075) -- the disturbance is NOT corrected at run end. The other three bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue) and base2 remained at their original rest poses throughout (verified in the same final snapshot), so only hex_red was affected.

Mechanism, per the executor's own diagnosis which matches my evidence: a grasp-center-offset orientation mismatch between hex_red's pick-step and place-step skill parameters produced a large orientation error on insertion attempts; after correcting the orientation the part still wasn't seated to full depth, and it slipped loose on release/retreat, ending up on the bench clear of its hole.

Because a standing violation (the undisturbed-bystander requirement over hex_red) remains uncorrected at the moment the run stopped, the run's end-state is non_conformant, even though the run's actual four-part objective (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow all seated) was achieved cleanly and even though the executor's own run_ended status is "aborted" rather than a success claim. The executor's diagnosis and mine agree, so this is not a disputed case -- but the record should note it is a non_conformant outcome driven entirely by an out-of-scope disturbance, not by any failure in the base1 assembly this task actually specifies.
